t: The Vedic period takes its name from the Vedas, liturgical texts composed and passed on by word of mouth in the northern Indian subcontinent between the end of the Indus cities and new cities of c. 600 BCE.
Early Vedic society was tribal and pastoral, centred in the Punjab; later, with iron tools, it settled the western Ganges Plain and formed kingdoms such as the Kuru.
The age produced fire sacrifice, the four varnas and the early Upanishads, and its tradition became one of the main parts of the later “Hindu synthesis”.
dyk: Horses, needed for cavalry and for sacrifice, could not be bred in India, so Vedic leaders kept up trade routes beyond the Hindu Kush to obtain them.
ev: The urban Indus Valley Civilisation collapses; in the mainstream view, Indo-Aryan groups then settle the northern Indus Valley
The Rigveda, the oldest layer of the Vedas, is composed
The Bharatas under their chief Sudas defeat a confederation of ten tribes in the Battle of the Ten Kings on the river Parushni (Ravi)
Vedic culture spreads east to the western Ganges Plain, and iron tools come into use
The early Kuru kingdom forms; Vedic hymns are collected and the Śrauta rituals developed
After the Kuru decline, the political centre of Vedic culture moves to Panchala under King Keśin Dālbhya
Videha rises under King Janaka, patron of the sages Yajnavalkya, Uddalaka Aruni and Gargi Vachaknavi
The Mahajanapadas, the first true cities and the śramaṇa movements, among them Jainism and Buddhism, mark the end of the period

f.homeland: The northern Indian subcontinent: first the Punjab and the northern Indus Valley, then from c. 1200–1000 BCE the western Ganges Plain (the Kuru-Panchala region and Ganga-Yamuna Doab), later Videha in northern Bihar and south-eastern Nepal
f.period: c. 1500–500 BCE: Early Vedic c. 1500–1000 BCE (the Rigveda composed c. 1400–1000 BCE); Later Vedic c. 1000–600 BCE (the Kuru, Panchala and Videha kingdoms); the Sutra texts to c. 500 BCE
f.known: the Vedas and early Upanishads; fire sacrifice (yajna) and Śrauta ritual; the gods Indra, Agni and Soma; the Kuru kingdom; the four varnas; the Ashvamedha horse sacrifice; the roots of dharma and karma
f.sources: The Vedic texts themselves, composed and orally transmitted with precision; the study of their language in five chronological layers; archaeological cultures linked with them (Ochre Coloured Pottery, Gandhara grave, Black and Red Ware, Painted Grey Ware); settlement surveys
